essays.title: The same conversations
essays.headline: The same conversations
essays.description: Product managers often stall not because they lack skill, but because their strengths go unchecked — helpfulness becomes overcommitment, diligence becomes output theatre, and loyalty becomes stagnation. And often the real cause is not the PM at all.
essays.llmsTitle: The Same Conversations: Why Good Product Managers Get Stuck
essays.llmsDesc: The three problems that recur in product careers — can't say no, mistakes activity for impact, stays too long — are virtues (helpfulness, diligence, loyalty) grown past their station, and the cure is subtraction. The deeper cause is often not the PM but a leadership team that never accepted that most of product work (discovery, measurement, coordination, rollout) is invisible. Covers prioritisation and saying no, output vs outcome, and when to leave a PM job.
